name: Orrath Hibiscus-Miso Stim Chews
description: Dense synth-chew tablets delivering a mild adenosine-blocker compound alongside a complex hibiscus-miso flavor profile. Each chew releases a slow burn of clarity over twenty minutes.
flavor_profile: Floral hibiscus tartness layered over umami miso depth, with a clean stimulant warmth that isn't bitter
cultural_context: Marketed at Tier 2-3 workers pulling double shifts, Orrath Stim Chews occupy the grey space between food and pharmaceutical. Technically legal, but some transit authorities restrict them in operating booths, making them a small rebellion for drivers and dock workers who chew them openly.
story_hooks: A batch of Orrath Stim Chews from a specific production run is causing users to experience vivid shared visual hallucinations — and NutraCorp is quietly buying back stock rather than issuing a recall.
A Tier 1 dealer is cutting street stims with Orrath compound, producing a much stronger and unpredictable effect that's spreading through the Shelf.
An Orrath quality control worker discovers the adenosine-blocker formula was modified six months ago without regulatory filing — and the modification wasn't an accident.
